Durham by the numbers

Which Durham offices send my property tax bill?

One county department does the work for the whole city. Durham County Tax Administration lists property, assesses it and collects the money, while the City of Durham decides only its own rate. In person, go to 201 East Main Street, 3rd Floor, Administration Building II, Durham, NC 27701, any weekday from 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM, or call 919-560-0300.

The county's own page splits the department into six areas: License and Fees, Payment and Collections, Personal Property, Real Property, Tax Help and Tax Relief. Mailed payments go to Durham County Tax Collector, PO Box 3397, Durham, NC 27702-3397, and the county asks residents never to mail cash. In foreclosure suits the plaintiffs are the City and County of Durham, which shows how closely the two governments share collection.

What combined tax rate applies to a home inside Durham city limits?

For fiscal year 2026-27 the county prints $0.4371 for the city and $0.5792 for the county, a combined $1.0163. The City of Durham's own budget news confirms the city piece at 43.71 cents per $100 of assessed value.

City and county rates for three fiscal years, as listed on the county's Tax Rates page

2026-2027$0.4371$0.5792$1.0163

The county reappraised real property effective January 1, 2025, and the second row is the first year printed after that change. A parcel inside the City of Durham Business Improvement District carries a combined rate of $1.0863 for 2026-27. The same page prints a solid waste fee of $185.00 for the 2026-27 year, plus separate lines for Morrisville, Cary, Raleigh and Chapel Hill.

Budget adoption wraps up in mid to late June, and new rates start July 1. The city's adopted 2026-27 budget totals $767 million, holds the property tax rate where it was, and raises water and sewer rates 12% for the average customer. Stormwater and parking rates did not change.

What dates matter for paying Durham property tax?

Tax is billed with a September 1 due date, yet the county gives you until January 5 before interest starts. From January 6, interest runs 2% for month one and three quarters of one percent per month afterward, following G.S. 105-360.

  • If the fifth lands on a Saturday or Sunday, paying the next business day is still on time.
  • Monthly plans cover real property only and must be set up before the bill goes delinquent.
  • Escrow accounts usually send their payment in late November.
  • Cards add a processing fee, while online electronic checks cost nothing.
  • A bounced check brings a $25 penalty, after which only cash or certified funds are taken.

How can a Durham owner challenge a new assessed value?

File with the county before its Board of Equalization and Review stops taking appeals. The 2026 cutoff was June 17 at 5:00 p.m., and it has passed. The county favors the online appeal on its Tax Help page, which lets you message staff and track your case, with a paper form as the fallback.

Durham appraised all real estate as of January 1, 2025. Staff say they can speak only to the appraised value, leaving the size of an increase, affordability and service levels aside. Between reappraisals the county may adjust a parcel only for events such as rezoning or a change to the buildings. A homeowner who loses before the county board has 30 days from the mailing of the decision to notify the state Property Tax Commission, per G.S. 105-290.

What relief programs does Durham County list for homeowners?

The Tax Relief page describes three homestead programs plus help through the county Department of Social Services for low income owners. Applications are due June 1, and the county invites calls at 919-560-0300.

  • An elderly or disabled exclusion with a one time application and a $38,800 income cap.
  • A circuit breaker deferment that holds tax to a percentage of income and needs a fresh application each year.
  • A disabled veteran exclusion of up to $45,000 of appraised value.

The county adds that deferred circuit breaker tax is repaid when the owner dies, sells or moves, with the most recent three years due. That makes a sale the moment to ask the assessor for the deferred balance.

What can Durham County do when a property tax bill goes unpaid?

Unpaid real property tax is a lien, and the county may hire private attorneys to foreclose under G.S. 105-374 after notices and a pre-foreclosure letter. The owner of record on the delinquency date, January 6, appears in a required newspaper notice, and a payment plan does not prevent that.

  • Bank attachment: the bank freezes accounts for ten days or until the tax office confirms payment.
  • Wage garnishment: the statutory deduction is 10% of gross pay each period.
  • State refund setoff: the state adds a $5.00 fee and a $15.00 administrative fee.
  • Sheriff levy: personal property can be seized and sold, with a $75.00 towing fee when a vehicle is taken.

After assignment to an attorney, the tax office stops accepting direct payments, and the payoff must cover taxes, interest, fees and costs through the attorney. Auctions run monthly on the second Tuesday at 12:00pm in the lobby of the Durham County Judicial Building, 510 Dillard Street. The high bidder deposits 10%, then an upset bid window stays open for 10 days. Redemption by the owner remains possible until the court confirms the sale. Durham County sells no tax liens, since the legislature ended that in 1983.

How does Durham property tax change what I do when I sell?

Whoever owned the parcel on January 1 is billed for that year, and a former owner is told to pass a stray bill to the buyer. Have your closing attorney explain how the year is shared, and get a written balance from the tax collector before choosing a closing date.

If the parcel has already gone to a foreclosure attorney, only that attorney can quote a payoff. Plan the closing date around that quote. Owners with deferred circuit breaker tax should ask the assessor for the figure that comes due on transfer.

How large is Durham and what do homes cost there?

The Census Bureau's city profile gives the base that these tax rates apply to.

  • 305,561 residents on the July 2025 estimate, a 7.6% rise over the 2020 base.
  • 112.79 square miles of land, which works out to 2,513.6 residents per square mile at the 2020 count.
  • Owners live in 52.3% of homes, and those homes have a median value of $392,800.
  • Middle household income of $81,619, with gross rent in the middle at $1,508.
  • 126,550 households of about 2.21 people each.

More questions about Durham, NC Property Tax Guide

What is the deadline to pay Durham property tax without interest?

January 5. Billing starts with a September 1 due date, and interest begins on January 6. A weekend January 5 pushes the cutoff to Monday, and registered vehicles follow their own schedule.

Does the Durham City Council set the property tax rate?

The council sets the city share through the budget it adopts each June, and the county commissioners set the county share. The two combine on one bill, and new rates take effect July 1.

Can I get a payment plan for my Durham property tax?

Yes for real property bills, if you arrange it before the bill turns delinquent. Until January 5 you can also pay in pieces with no formal agreement.

If I sold my Durham house in March, who owes that year's bill?

The county bills the owner of record on January 1, even after a sale. It advises forwarding the bill to the new owner, so settle the split with your closing attorney.

How do I stop a Durham tax foreclosure?

Contact the attorney assigned to the parcel for a redemption figure and pay taxes, interest, fees and costs before the court confirms the sale. A federal bankruptcy filing can also halt the process.

Challenging your assessment

Real property: appeal to the Board of Equalization and Review (BER) under G.S. 105-322 by filing a Formal Appeal Form with the County Office of Tax Administration no later than the BER adjournment date (May 4, 2026 for the 2026 cycle; exception for notice-of-value-change recipients: later of adjournment or the 'Last Date to Appeal' on the notice). File by email (Appeals@MeckNC.gov), mail (PO Box 31127, Charlotte NC 28231) or in person (3205 Freedom Dr, Suite 3500). Supporting documents. See the official page.

Local notes

  • Charlotte, Cornelius, Huntersville, Matthews and Mint Hill city/town taxes are billed together with county tax on the Mecklenburg bill and collected by the County Tax Collector (page opened).
  • Census Vintage 2025 population 964784; primary county Mecklenburg County from Census SUMLEV 157.

Charlotte by the numbers

Who values and bills property tax in Charlotte?

Mecklenburg County's Office of Tax Administration values every parcel in Charlotte and collects the county's tax, and the City of Charlotte's own property tax rides on the same bill. The county's rate page says a total bill includes a municipal tax from Charlotte or one of the six county towns, plus county and municipal solid waste fees where they apply. Payments go to the City-County Tax Collector.

The office's own description covers valuing parcels, collecting ad valorem and business gross receipts taxes, and running relief programs. Appeals, relief applications and the revaluation all run through the county. City Council's part is the city rate, which it sets in its yearly budget.

Payment options on the county page include a toll-free card line at 1-800-994-1026 that answers day and night, mailed checks to Charlotte post office boxes, bank eCheck payments, and counter service during weekday office hours. A payment with no 24-digit bill number in the account box is rejected and returned. Cards carry a vendor fee of $3.95 on Visa or Mastercard debit and 2.35 percent (minimum $1.95) on other cards, while eChecks carry none. A bank-initiated payment can take up to four business days to post.

What are the Charlotte property tax rates and key dates?

The Mecklenburg County rate is 49.27 cents on each $100 of value, and the county adopted its FY2027 budget on June 2, 2026 with that rate unchanged. The city rate comes on top of it for property inside Charlotte, and the figure for a given year appears on your bill and in the city budget. The table lists the items that matter most to a seller.

Charlotte and Mecklenburg County property tax figures from official county and city pages

County rate, FY2026 and FY202749.27 cents per $100County tax rates page; FY2027 budget news release

City Manager presented the proposal on May 4, 2026, with a Council vote slated for June 8. Look to the city's budget pages for what Council finally adopted. On the state calendar, a bill is due September 1 and stays interest-free through January 5.

What is the route for contesting a Charlotte tax value?

You file a Formal Appeal Form with the county Office of Tax Administration, and the board of equalization and review hears it. In a normal year the deadline is the board's adjournment date, which was May 4, 2026 for the most recent cycle. The only exception is for owners who receive a notice of value change, who may file by the later of adjournment or the last date to appeal on the notice.

  • File by email to the county's appeals address, by mail to Mecklenburg County BER Real Property Appeals, P.O. Box 31127, Charlotte, NC 28231, or in person at 3205 Freedom Dr, Suite 3500, Charlotte, NC 28208.
  • Back-up documents must arrive with the form or within 45 days of filing it. Anyone other than you or an attorney who speaks for you needs a signed power of attorney.
  • Expect the hearing notice roughly a month before your slot, and send any request to reschedule in writing within ten days of that notice.
  • The board's ruling comes by mail within a month of the hearing. If you disagree, the Property Tax Commission in Raleigh takes the next appeal, and you have 30 days to file it.

The burden sits with the owner, who must show the tax value substantially exceeds market value. No revaluation-year appeal can be filed before notices of value go out, and the county expects the notices and refreshed online records in early 2027.

Between revaluations, the county keeps the prior value unless a ground in G.S. 105-287(a) applies. The county lists clerical or arithmetic mistakes, a misapplied schedule of values, physical changes to the land or buildings, and a change in legal use.

Does Charlotte offer property tax relief for homeowners?

Yes. Mecklenburg County runs the state homestead programs from its tax relief page, and its FY2027 budget carries $3.5 million for the county's HOMES program, described as relief for qualifying homeowners. A Charlotte owner applies to the county for all of them, and the tax office contact page lists a mailbox for real estate relief questions.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: removes half of a home's appraised value, or $25,000 if that is more, for owners aged 65 and up or permanently and totally disabled whose income stays within the cap (NCDOR printed $38,800 for 2026).
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: removes $45,000 of appraised value through Form NCDVA-9, whatever the owner's age or income.
  • Circuit breaker: defers the part of the bill above 4 or 5 percent of income, depending on where income falls between the cap and $58,200. The deferred amount is a lien and, on a transfer, comes due together with the prior three years.

The county page defines income broadly, counting every source except family gifts and inheritances. File Form AV-9 with the county, which has to take applications up to June 1 ahead of the tax year.

Who settles the Charlotte tax bill when a house sells?

Any balance gets cleared from sale proceeds at closing, because the debt rides with the parcel. The lien arises on January 1, so a house sold in March already owes that year's tax even though the September 1 due date has not arrived. Treat that year's amount as a payoff line.

After January 5 a bill starts accruing interest, 2 percent for the rest of January and three-fourths of a percent per month after that. Prolonged nonpayment lets the county file a court action modeled on mortgage foreclosure, with an auction sale. An owner can redeem ahead of confirmation by paying everything owed. The tax office site also hosts a Delinquent Taxpayer Lists page.

On the deed side, the seller (transferor) pays North Carolina's excise tax to the Mecklenburg County register of deeds before the deed is recorded. Your closing attorney can confirm the stamps and filing charges that will show on the settlement statement.

What does Charlotte look like for a house seller?

Census Bureau figures show Charlotte at 964,784 people for July 1, 2025, a 10.3 percent rise over the 2020 base. The land area is 308.29 square miles, with 2,836.9 residents per square mile in 2020. Owners occupy 51.0 percent of homes, which leaves renters with almost half.

Over 2020-2024 the typical owned home was valued at $385,700, gross rent at a median of $1,612 and household income at a median of $82,068. Roughly 48.0 percent of adults over 25 hold at least a bachelor's degree, and workers average a 24.7-minute trip to work. The city's FY2027 budget also counts on a new voter-approved sales tax for mobility.

The 2027 values will draw on four years of sales since 2023. A seller listing in early 2027 should watch for the notice mailing, since the new assessment shapes later tax bills and a buyer may ask about it.

More questions about Charlotte, NC Property Tax Guide

What is the property tax rate in Charlotte?

The county levy is 49.27 cents on each $100 of value, and the FY2027 budget left it alone. Charlotte adds its own city rate to that for property inside the city, set by City Council each year. Your bill shows both, along with any solid waste fee.

When is the next Charlotte revaluation?

The next one lands in 2027. Mecklenburg County moved to a four-year cycle, and the previous revaluation was 2023. Notices and updated online records are expected in early 2027, and the county's page invites an informal review request within 30 days of the notice date.

How do I pay a Charlotte property tax bill?

Use the card line at 1-800-994-1026, send an eCheck, mail a check to the City-County Tax Collector, or visit during weekday hours. Whatever you choose, include the 24-digit bill number, since a payment without it is returned. Cards bring a vendor fee.

Can I appeal my Charlotte property value after the deadline?

Not for the 2026 cycle. Requests had to be in by May 4, 2026, unless a notice of value change gave you a later last date. The next broad opening follows the 2027 revaluation notices.

What happens to unpaid Charlotte property tax when I sell?

It comes out of your proceeds at closing, with interest added if the bill is past January 5. The lien has attached to the parcel since January 1 of the tax year. Get the balance from the Mecklenburg Office of Tax Administration before you sign a contract.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Local notes

Behind on Raleigh property tax?

Get My Cash Offer →

Raleigh by the numbers

Which office bills a Raleigh homeowner?

Wake County does. Under a local agreement, its Tax Administration department sends the bills for Raleigh and the county's other towns, so a Raleigh owner receives one statement carrying county and city charges.

That department also values land, buildings and business property. Its phone line is 919-856-5400 and its email is taxhelp@wake.gov. The county tax bill pages also say Wake has 16 cities and towns, and a municipal rate is folded into each bill. Questions about how Raleigh set its own rate go to the city, not the county.

What rates apply to a Raleigh property tax bill?

Wake County's rate page prints a county rate of .5371 and a Raleigh rate of .3720, for a combined .9091 per $100 of value. Wake's 2026 bill page says county commissioners voted on June 1 to adopt a fiscal year 2027 budget that raises the county rate to 53.71 cents.

The county's own worked example for a house inside Raleigh and outside any fire or special district adds a $20 waste reduction fee. Where the parcel lies can add further lines:

  • Residential waste reduction fee, charged per living unit, so a duplex has two.
  • Fire district tax, where the property lies in one.
  • Special district tax, usually a downtown area designated by legislation.
  • Municipal fees such as stormwater or solid waste.
  • A vehicle fee for motor vehicles inside a municipality.

To see the exact charges for your address, use the county's online bill search or call the tax office.

Rates and fee example printed on the Wake County tax rates page
LineAs printed
Wake County rate.5371 per $100
City of Raleigh rate.3720 per $100
Combined rate.9091 per $100
Waste reduction fee in the county example$20

When are Raleigh property taxes due?

The county mails bills in July. Each one covers the fiscal year that starts July 1 and ends the next June 30. Payment at face amount is allowed from September 1 through January 5, as G.S. 105-360.

After that, interest runs. Wake's real estate page prints 2 percent for January and an added 0.75 percent per month after that. The county says it takes partial payments in any amount, with no prior approval, as long as the balance is paid in full by January 5. Short-term payment plans are possible, and the county advises calling early because it cannot help once a bill is overdue. Past-due taxes can be collected from paychecks, bank accounts or rent under state law.

Who gets billed when a Raleigh home changes hands mid-year?

The county explains it by sale date. If you sold between January and June and keep no interest in the property, the July bill should go to the new owner, who is responsible for paying it.

If the sale falls after the July bill and before the January delinquency date, the county mails a statement for the unpaid tax to the new owner, and the seller may disregard the original notice. Wake real estate becomes subject to a tax lien each January 1, and the lien stays until every dollar is paid. If a lender paid last year's bill from escrow, no July statement arrives, so look the account up online. Tell the closing attorney how you want that year's bill divided, and request the balance from Wake County Tax Administration.

Can Raleigh owners get a tax break?

Wake County names three state programs: senior and disabled, tax deferment, and disabled veteran. The county's tax relief pages explain who qualifies, and its 2026 bill page says the June 1 state deadline has passed but late applications can be accepted for good cause through December 31, 2026. Not knowing the program existed is typically not good cause.

The underlying laws are the senior and disabled statute and the veteran statute. Wake County Tax Administration can say whether a window is open.

How can you pay a Wake County tax bill in Raleigh?

Online, by several routes. The county's 2026 bill page lists ACH or eCheck, PayPal, Venmo, Apple Pay, Google Pay, and credit cards from the four major networks. Bills can be looked up online without waiting for the mail.

Owners with escrow accounts get no mailed bill; the county tells them to look online or call 919-856-5400. After each partial payment, Tax Administration sends a statement showing what remains.

When does Wake County revalue Raleigh property?

Wake's latest countywide revaluation carries a January 1, 2024 effective date, and the next one is dated January 1, 2027. In March 2025 the Wake County Board of Commissioners voted to phase in a two-year cycle, so the first revaluation on that cycle is effective January 1, 2029.

By the county's account, roughly 460,000 parcels are sorted into 5,400 neighborhoods that share market, economic and geographic traits. Appraisers price land and buildings from sales data, review the results in the field and the office, and compile them into a Schedule of Values that commissioners must approve. The state minimum is one revaluation every eight years, and the county says shorter gaps keep value increases from arriving as one large jump.

Which values and rates sit behind the bill due September 1, 2026?

The county explains that bills due September 1, 2026, and delinquent after January 5, 2027, rest on assessed values as of January 1, 2024, and the rates approved in June 2026. Bills due September 1, 2027 use values as of January 1, 2027 and the rates set in June 2027.

  • A bill is assessed value times a rate stated per $100 of value.
  • Revaluation changes values only. Elected county and town officials set the rate.
  • State law has local governments publish a revenue-neutral rate for comparison, though they need not adopt it.
  • The county's online real estate search shows your current value and the data behind it.

What if my Wake County value or property record looks wrong?

The county plans to mail 2027 value notices in the week of January 19, 2027, when commissioners receive the results. Every owner may appeal to the county's review board, and instructions plus a portal link are due out in January 2027.

If the record itself is wrong, for example a wrong square footage figure or an outbuilding that is gone, file the county's online request form with your address or account number and any documents. An appraiser may need to visit, and you would be contacted. Tax Administration also plans a comparable sales tool in January, useful as evidence. The next level above the local board is the state commission, covered in G.S. 105-290.

How should a Raleigh seller deal with unpaid property tax?

Get the balance in writing from Wake County Tax Administration and hand it to your closing attorney. An unpaid bill follows the house, so it has to be settled for the title to be clean.

Back taxes can be cleared out of a seller's proceeds at the sale. Another option is a payment plan before the January deadline. A direct cash purchase of a Raleigh house as-is can move quickly while interest runs. Whoever buys, have the payoff quote cover the day you close.

More questions about Raleigh, NC Property Tax Guide

Will Raleigh mail me a separate city tax bill?

No. A local agreement has Wake County collect the city's share together with its own, so the single bill comes from Wake County Tax Administration.

When does a late Raleigh bill begin to accrue interest?

Interest starts January 6 if the bill is not paid in full by January 5. The county prints 2 percent for January and 0.75 percent per month after that.

Does Wake County take installments?

Yes. Any partial amount is welcome with no prior approval, so long as the full balance is in by January 5. Payment plans are possible if you call early.

What rates are printed for Raleigh on the Wake County page?

The county rate page prints .5371 for Wake County and .3720 for Raleigh, a combined .9091 per $100 of value. Fees and district taxes may add to your bill, so check your own account.

Who owes the July bill if I sold my Raleigh house in the spring?

If you sold between January and June and keep no interest, the county says the new owner should receive the July bill and is responsible for paying it. Confirm at closing.

Appeal to the Board of Equalization and Review: annual appeal window Jan 1 through May 15, 5 p.m. (next business day if weekend/holiday); per Senate Bill 889 appeals for tax year 2026 may be submitted through Dec 31, 2026; tax year 2027 appeals through May 17, 2027 with online portal opening Jan 1, 2027. Written appeal, online or paper form (336-641-4814).. See the official page.

Greensboro by the numbers

Who bills property tax for a Greensboro home?

Guilford County, not the City of Greensboro, sends the bill, and the city levy rides on the same statement. The Guilford County Tax Department keeps counters at 400 W. Market St. in Greensboro and 325 E. Russell Ave. in High Point, both staffed 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Friday.

Dial 336-641-4814 about values and appeals. The county's FAQ names 336-641-3363 for anyone who wants to arrange paying a balance in full before the delinquent date. Greensboro sets its own levy, and the county's table shows it on a separate line.

Lenders that escrow ask the county for your bill each summer and mail you a notice. Under North Carolina law, getting the tax paid stays the owner's job, so if the lender named on that notice is not yours, pass it to the correct servicer.

What property tax rates apply inside Greensboro?

The county's 2026-2027 rate page prints a countywide rate of 0.78950 and a City of Greensboro rate of 0.79850, for a total of 1.58800 under rate code 01. The county explains that its rates are fractions of $1 for each $100 of value.

Guilford County 2026-2027 rates for Greensboro parcels, as the county prints them (https://guilfordcountync.gov/government/departments-and-agencies/tax-department/2026-2027-tax-property-rates)

Code 01 covers most city parcels. Parcels in the Dunleath and College Hill historic districts and the downtown improvement district carry an extra district charge, so read the code on your bill. A $30 vehicle fee also applies in Greensboro, and the county says it is neither discounted nor penalized.

How did Senate Bill 889 change Greensboro property tax bills?

It froze the use of the 2026 reappraisal values for one year, so bills for the fiscal year that began July 1, 2026 rest on the older values. The City of Greensboro says the moratorium applies to the county's revaluation process and does not stop local governments from changing their rates.

  • Greensboro adopted its fiscal year 2026-27 budget on June 16, with a total city rate of 79.85 cents.
  • The city describes that as a 12.6-cent adjustment on current property values, not on the new reappraisal values.
  • The county says the updated values are paused until January 1, 2027, and are expected to feed the budget year that begins July 1, 2027.

The practical result: your new notice of value does not set this year's bill. It still matters, because if the value is wrong, the appeal clock runs on it, and an appeal that stays open now is considered for the 2027 tax year.

When are Greensboro property taxes due, and how can I pay?

The due date is September 1, and a bill stays free of interest through January 5 (G.S. 105-360). The county's FAQ then charges 2% for the first month and adds 0.75% on the first of every month that follows.

  • Discount: Guilford County and Greensboro give 1.0% off for payment before September 1, per the county rate page.
  • Online, or by phone at (336) 203-7795: 1.85% processing charge and a $2 transaction fee.
  • At a tax office counter: cash and checks are free, while a card carries 2.35% and $2.
  • Mail: Guilford County Tax Department, P.O. Box 70939, Charlotte, NC 28272-0939.

The USPS postmark fixes the date of a mailed payment, and proving it was on time falls to the taxpayer. The county says it phones about payment only when a bill is delinquent, and gift cards are never accepted.

What is the process for appealing a Greensboro value?

Send it to the Guilford County Tax Department. The county's appeals page accepts 2026 filings through December 31, 2026, and 2027 filings through May 17, 2027, when the online portal opens January 1, 2027.

An owner who already appealed the reappraisal value does not need to refile, because that appeal carries into tax year 2027. The deadline originally published was May 15, 2026, at 5 p.m.

For a paper form, the county advises handing it to a postal clerk for a hand-cancelled postmark, since a mailbox drop can be stamped the next day with no proof. Anything postmarked after May 17 is rejected. Before the portal opens, a form can be requested at taxreval@guilfordcountync.gov.

The board hears whatever staff cannot settle, and the next stop is the state Property Tax Commission, with notice due 30 days after the board mails its decision (G.S. 105-290). Personal property is a separate track with its own 30-day window from the notice date.

What tax relief can Greensboro homeowners apply for?

Greensboro homeowners may use any of three state programs, with a June 1 filing deadline each year. Mail applications to Guilford County Tax Department, PO Box 3138, Greensboro, NC 27402, or carry them to either tax office.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: $25,000 or half the value, whichever is more, off the home of a qualifying 65-plus or disabled owner whose gross income stays under $38,800 on the county's page. One application is enough.
  • Circuit breaker: the tax is held to 4% or 5% of income, using the printed caps of $38,800 and $58,200, after five years of owning and living in the home. It is renewed annually.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of value, with no age or income test, applied for once.

Only one program per owner is allowed. The county will still review a late application if it arrives at least one week before the last equalization board meeting in December. Questions go to 336-641-3320 or 336-641-7911. A circuit breaker owner who sells owes the last three years of deferred tax, with interest, on the sale date.

What happens when Greensboro property tax goes unpaid before a sale?

Interest starts, collection begins at once, and the tax remains a lien on the parcel. The county's FAQ lists wage and bank garnishment, levies on personal property, attachment of state refunds and lottery winnings, and foreclosure on real estate.

Under G.S. 105-355 the lien dates from the listing date and includes penalties and costs. A foreclosure action under G.S. 105-374 ends at a courthouse-door auction, and redemption before confirmation requires paying taxes, interest, penalties and costs. The county says it holds no tax lien sales.

Before listing, ask the tax department for the figures on the current bill. A deferred balance under a relief program is a separate item, so ask for it by name.

How big is Greensboro and who lives in its homes?

QuickFacts shows Greensboro at 308,667 people in 2025, compared with 299,035 in the 2020 Census and 269,666 in 2010. The city occupies about 130 square miles of land, which works out to about 2,308 people for each.

  • Households: 123,984, averaging 2.29 people (2020 to 2024).
  • Owner-occupied homes: 50.5%.
  • Value of the typical owner's home: $244,800.
  • Typical gross rent: $1,172.
  • Typical household income: $61,515.
  • Average commute: 21.7 minutes.
  • Adults with a bachelor's degree or more: 41.0%.

Owners and renters are nearly even, so a Greensboro sale often has a landlord on one side. Typical monthly owner costs with a mortgage are $1,447, which gives a baseline to hold against your own tax line.

More questions about Greensboro, NC Property Tax Guide

Which government mails the Greensboro tax statement?

Guilford County. Its tax department bills the county and city levies together from counters at 400 W. Market St., Greensboro, and 325 E. Russell Ave., High Point.

What total rate does a city parcel carry?

Rate code 01 totals 1.58800 in the county's 2026-2027 table, made of 0.78950 countywide plus 0.79850 for Greensboro. Historic and downtown districts add more.

Does Greensboro reward early payers?

Yes. Guilford County and Greensboro each allow a 1.0% discount for paying before September 1, according to the rate page.

Is an appeal still possible after the moratorium?

Yes. Guilford accepts 2026 appeals through December 31, 2026, and 2027 appeals through May 17, 2027, with its online portal starting January 1, 2027. Earlier appeals stay active.

Does Guilford County auction tax liens to investors?

No. The tax department says it conducts no tax lien sales, though it enforces collection with garnishment and real estate foreclosure.

Winston Salem by the numbers

Which office handles property tax for a Winston-Salem home?

Winston-Salem property owners deal with Forsyth County Tax Administration, which takes appeals, relief applications and ownership questions. Stop by 201 N. Chestnut Street, home of the Forsyth County Government Center, or phone 336-703-2300. A first visit goes faster with the parcel number in hand, and the same counter issues the appeal and relief forms.

The county's real estate page says its appraisal section can answer value questions faster if you have the parcel number, the owner's full name and the street address ready. Appraisal records can be bought for 50 cents a page. Ask the tax office how any city levy appears on your bill, since this page states no rate.

What does the Winston-Salem housing market look like?

Census estimates 257,271 residents for 2025, QuickFacts. That is up 3.1% above the 249,549 base counted in April 2020, spread across roughly 133 square miles.

  • Owner-occupied homes make up 55.6% of housing for 2020 to 2024, which leaves nearly half the homes in rental use.
  • Census lists $233,800 as the typical owned home's value and $1,087 as gross rent.
  • Households earn a median $59,268, and workers spend 21.5 minutes getting to work.
  • About 39.5% of adults aged 25 or older have finished a four-year program.

These are city-wide figures, so a house on one street can sit far from the averages, and a house needing repairs may carry an assessed value higher than its likely sale price. That mismatch is a reason to review the assessment before listing.

When are Winston-Salem property taxes due?

North Carolina law makes taxes due September 1 and lets owners pay at face value through the day before January 6, per G.S. 105-360. After that, interest of 2% runs through the start of February and then three-fourths of a percent for each month.

One line on the county's real estate page matters for sellers: the bill is issued to the January 1 titleholder, and selling later in the year leaves that seller liable. Closings normally prorate the tax, and the county suggests checking with your realtor or attorney that this was done.

Mailed payments count on their USPS postmark date under the same statute.

What is the window to challenge a Winston-Salem value?

Send the county's review board a written appeal. The county's real estate page says it must arrive or be postmarked after January 1 and no later than the last business day in June.

For 2026 the county announced June 30 as the real property appeal deadline, and that date is behind us. The form is online and at the Tax Office, and it goes to the board that sits under G.S. 105-322.

A reappraisal year can shift the calendar, so confirm with the office before filing.

What tax relief can a Winston-Salem owner apply for?

Forsyth County names three relief programs, and an owner may use just one. A May 2026 county notice gave June 1, 2026 as that year's filing deadline, and the NCDOR form describes the same June 1 cutoff.

North Carolina relief programs as described in Forsyth County's May 2026 notice

The statutes behind these are G.S. 105-277.1 and G.S. 105-277.1B. The county's notice adds that the circuit breaker is aimed at owners with several non-spouse owners who all meet the standards, and applications come from the Tax Office or online.

What if there is back tax on a Winston-Salem house?

Debt travels with the land. Under G.S. 105-355, a lien attaches on the January 1 listing date, with penalties, interest and costs added at the same time.

Collection can reach a court-ordered sale. Selling first avoids that, and the closing agent settles the amount from proceeds.

  • Get the exact balance for the parcel from the county.
  • Have the attorney show it on the settlement sheet, and keep the receipt with your closing papers in case a question comes up later.
  • Keep proof of payment for your records.

How has Winston-Salem grown?

The city's population went from 229,617 in the 2010 census to 249,545 in 2020, and Census estimates 257,271 for July 2025. The 2020 density was about 1,880 residents on each square mile of its 132.7 square miles of land. These figures describe the city alone, so owners elsewhere in Forsyth County may see different numbers on their own records.

Other QuickFacts for the city include 10,986 veterans for 2020 to 2024, a 17.7% poverty rate, and 85.3% of residents unchanged in address over the prior year, a sign of a fairly settled population. Veterans whose disability meets the state test may qualify for the $45,000 disabled veteran exclusion, and the Tax Office can explain the steps.

The Census median for monthly owner costs is $1,459 with a mortgage and $486 without. A seller comparing the cost of holding a vacant house should add the tax bill, insurance and upkeep to those figures, since the Census cost line is an average for occupied homes.

How do circuit breaker deferrals affect a sale in Winston-Salem?

A deferral becomes a lien, so it has to be cleared when the house sells. Under the circuit breaker program, the part of the tax above the income cap is deferred, and the county's notice says that amount accrues interest and is added to the property as a lien.

Owners who qualify should ask the Tax Office for the full deferred balance before listing. It shows up in the title search, and the closing agent pays it from the seller's proceeds. The program also requires five years of owning and occupying the home, and a new application each year, as the NCDOR form states.

  • Income of $38,800 or less pays 4% of income under the county's 2026 notice.
  • Income above that, up to $58,200, pays 5% of income.
  • Any tax above those amounts is deferred and carries interest.

How should a seller in Winston-Salem plan around tax dates?

Line up your closing with the tax year. A spring closing happens after the date that fixed the owner, so the seller's name sits on that year's bill even when the buyer moves in during March.

An inherited or empty house follows the same rule, and unpaid amounts keep growing through interest. If you want to challenge the value, file by the final business day of June, which means deciding before you list.

More questions about Winston-Salem, NC Property Tax Guide

Which number reaches Winston-Salem's tax office?

Call Forsyth County Tax Administration at 336-703-2300. The office is in the Forsyth County Government Center at 201 N. Chestnut Street.

When does a Winston-Salem appeal window end?

The county's real estate page names the last business day in June. In 2026 that was June 30, and it has passed, so check with the office about the year you are filing.

Will I owe tax after a spring sale?

Possibly. The bill carries the January 1 owner's name, and the closing normally splits the cost between buyer and seller.

When does interest start on unpaid Winston-Salem tax?

Interest starts on January 6 under G.S. 105-360, at 2% until February 1 and three-fourths of a percent per month after that.

Can I get a lower tax bill as a senior or veteran?

Maybe. All three state programs need an application and cannot be stacked. Ask whether you meet the age, disability or veteran tests, since the answer changes which one fits.

Maurice Braswell Courthouse) or drop box. Personal property: 30 days from bill date.. See the official page.

Fayetteville by the numbers

Who bills property tax in Fayetteville, NC?

One county office, Cumberland Tax Administration, sets the assessed value of a Fayetteville house and also mails the bill and takes the payment. The City of Fayetteville adopts its own rate, but the county puts both levies on a single bill.

The office sits at 117 Dick Street, Room 530, Fayetteville, NC 28301, and answers at 910-678-7507. Mail goes to Cumberland Tax Administration, PO Box 449, Fayetteville NC 28302. Most owners see the Fayetteville city rate, the county rate and any city fees stacked on one statement, which is why a closing agent asks for the parcel number before quoting a payoff.

The Census Bureau puts Fayetteville at 209,120 people on July 1, 2025, across 148.26 square miles of land. The county page on local history gives 661 square miles for the county and records that Campbellton took the name Fayetteville in 1783 and that a fire in 1831 burned most of the town. The county history traces the base now called Fort Bragg to a 1918 artillery camp.

What rates and fees show up on a Fayetteville tax bill?

A Fayetteville bill combines a county rate of 49.9 cents per $100 of value with a city rate of 44.95 cents per $100, plus flat fees for trash and stormwater.

The county's rate page covers the 2026 tax bills (fiscal year 2027). It prints each levy as a decimal, and the combined figure for the city is 0.9485. Unincorporated owners pay a different mix, including a fire district charge and a recreation rate, so a house just outside the city line is billed differently from one inside it.

Fayetteville levies as printed by Cumberland County for 2026 tax bills (source: county Tax Rates page)
ItemWhat the page prints
County ad valorem rate0.499
City of Fayetteville rate0.4495
Combined city and county rate0.9485
Fayetteville Revitalization District0.1489 + 0.4495, combined 1.0974
City solid waste fee, residential units with seven or fewer units$285 a year
City residential stormwater fee$84, $168 or $252 a year by impervious area tier
City vehicle fee and transit tax$25 and $5 per registered vehicle

The stormwater tiers turn on impervious surface. Tier 1 is under 2,500 square feet, tier 2 runs from 2,501 to 4,800 square feet, and tier 3 is anything larger. Two rules to remember:

  • The combined rate on the page leaves out stormwater, solid waste, refuse, recycling and transit charges, so the real bill is higher than the rate alone suggests.
  • Parcels inside the revitalization district carry an added levy on top of the city rate.

What is the payment calendar for a Fayetteville bill?

Cumberland bills carry a September 1 due date, and the rate page puts the interest-free cutoff at January 5.

G.S. 105-360 sets that rhythm for the whole state. A payment that arrives before January 6 costs only the face amount. From January 6 until February 1, a 2 percent charge applies, and after that the account gains three-fourths of one percent for every month or part of a month. The county's 2025 revaluation calendar listed August for mailing that year's bills, and owners who cannot pay all at once can phone 910-678-7507 to arrange installments.

Ask the closing attorney whether the payoff covers the current-year bill. Because the lien follows the parcel to its next owner, an unpaid balance does not vanish at the deed. The lien rules are in G.S. 105-355.

How did the 2025 revaluation change Fayetteville assessments?

Every parcel in Cumberland County was reappraised to its January 1, 2025 market value, replacing values set in 2017.

The county's revaluation page says the last prior reappraisal took effect January 1, 2017, and cites the state requirement that counties reappraise at least once every eight years. It describes the goal as equity between properties, with no intent to raise or lower total tax. Notices went out February 21, 2025, and the new rates took effect July 1, 2025 once the county and the city adopted their budgets.

Relief approvals carry over. The county's page says previously approved tax relief applications stay valid and nobody has to refile after revaluation. Its FAQ adds that an exemption's approval stays in place while the billed amount moves with the new value.

Where do I send a challenge to my Fayetteville value?

Send an informal Request for Review to Tax Administration first, and carry any open dispute to the Board of Equalization and Review.

  • Informal review: submit online, by mail, by email, at Room 530 of the county courthouse at 117 Dick Street, or through the secure drop box in the back parking lot. Attach evidence such as comparable sales.
  • Deadline: the county's page lists February 5, 2027 for informal appeals on the 2027 tax year, and a decision letter follows around April 2027.
  • Board hearing: the 2026 Board of Equalization and Review adjourned May 20, 2026, which closed that year's window.
  • Further appeal: the state Property Tax Commission takes a written notice filed inside 30 days of the board's mailed ruling (G.S. 105-290).

Informal requests by mail go to Cumberland Tax Administration, Attn: Real Estate Assessment, PO Box 449, Fayetteville NC 28302. Give a working phone number and mailing address, because an appraiser may schedule a visit to the house.

Can a Fayetteville homeowner shrink the bill with a relief program?

Three state programs exist, and each owner can draw from just one: a senior or disability exclusion, a disabled veteran exclusion and a circuit breaker cap.

  • Senior or disabled owners with 2026 income at or below $38,800 shield at least $25,000 of value, or half the value when that figure is larger (G.S. 105-277.1).
  • Disabled veterans shield $45,000 of value, regardless of age or income (G.S. 105-277.1C).
  • The circuit breaker holds the bill to 4 percent of income, or 5 percent for income between $38,800 and $58,200, and defers the remainder as a lien (G.S. 105-277.1B).

Apply on Form AV-9 at the county assessor's office, preferably in January and no later than June 1 before the tax year. Cumberland says earlier approvals remain valid after the 2025 revaluation. Selling the house ends a circuit breaker deferral, and three years of deferred tax then fall due.

What if I list or sell a Fayetteville house while tax is unpaid?

The balance is cleared from sale proceeds at the table, since the lien attached to the parcel on the January 1 listing date.

Get a written payoff from the county that includes interest and city fees, then pass it to the closing attorney. A bill left unpaid after January 5 can end in a court foreclosure of the lien. G.S. 105-374 describes a public auction at the courthouse door, and a person redeeming before confirmation pays taxes, penalties, interest and costs. A prompt sale avoids that route, because the payoff comes out of the price.

The local market adds context. The Census Bureau counts 82,689 households in the city, and only 47.4 percent of homes are owned by their occupants (2020 to 2024), with a median owner-occupied value of $188,000. With median gross rent at $1,250, a share of sellers are landlords, and a rented house carries the same lien as any other.

More questions about Fayetteville, NC Property Tax Guide

Which office answers questions about a Fayetteville property tax bill?

Cumberland County Tax Administration, at 910-678-7507 or 117 Dick Street, Room 530. It handles assessment, billing and payment arrangements for Fayetteville owners.

When does interest begin on an unpaid Fayetteville bill?

January 6. The county tells owners to pay by January 5, and under state law a 2 percent charge runs to February 1, followed by three-fourths of one percent each month.

What combined rate applies inside Fayetteville city limits?

The county's 2026 rate page prints 0.9485, built from 0.4495 for the city and 0.499 for the county. Solid waste, stormwater and vehicle charges are added separately.

Is it too late to appeal my Fayetteville value?

Not for the 2027 tax year. The county lists February 5, 2027 as the informal deadline, with the Board of Equalization and Review taking formal appeals afterward. The 2026 board adjourned May 20, 2026.

Does the unpaid tax stay with the house after a sale?

Yes, the lien stays on the parcel and follows it to the buyer. Sellers usually clear it at closing through the closing attorney.

Which government bills a Cary home for property tax?

The county does, not the town. The Town of Cary says its limits now span three counties, Wake, Chatham and Durham, and that each county handles assessment, valuation, billing and collection for the town's tax.

Your parcel's location decides which of the three applies, and the bill itself or a county online search will tell you. The town page lists the numbers it wants residents to use:

  • Wake County Tax Administration, 919-856-5400. In-person help is at 301 S. McDowell St., Suite 3800, in Raleigh, weekdays from 8:30 in the morning to 5:00.
  • Chatham County Collection Division, 919-542-8250.
  • Durham County Tax Administrator, 919-560-0300.

Wake's page describes the arrangement: by local agreement the county sends the bills and collects the money for municipal and special districts within its borders. A Cary owner in Wake therefore pays one bill with the county and town rates together, and anyone with questions about how the town rate was set is told to ask the town. The town also adds a $30 vehicle license fee that rides on the vehicle tax bill, with no sticker.

What are the Cary and Wake County tax rates?

For fiscal year 2027 the official pages print 36.75 cents per $100 for the town and 53.71 cents per $100 for Wake County. Both are stated as printed on the official budget pages, and a bill adds the two when the parcel is in Wake.

The Cary Town Council adopted its budget at the regular meeting on June 25, 2026, raising the town rate by 2.75 cents. The same budget sets a solid waste and recycling fee of $28 per month, which is a town charge listed separately from the property tax rate. Wake's commissioners voted on June 1 for a 2-cent increase to reach 53.71 cents.

Both rates apply to the assessed value, so the value matters as much as the rate. Revaluation changes values, and the rate that follows can move in either direction. Chatham and Durham County parcels carry those counties' own rates, which you can get from the numbers above. Rates reset every July 1 with the budgets, so confirm them on the current bill instead of relying on last year's figure.

When are Cary property taxes due?

The due date is September 1, and a payment through January 5 owes nothing extra; interest begins January 6 under G.S. 105-360.

StepRuleSource
Listing periodFirst business day of January through January 31G.S. 105-307
Taxes dueSeptember 1G.S. 105-360
No interestThrough January 5G.S. 105-360 and Wake County
Interest charge2% for the stretch from January 6 to February 1, then three-fourths of a percent per monthG.S. 105-360
Relief applicationDeadline June 1, with late filing for good cause considered case by caseWake County

Wake lets owners make partial payments of any size without prior approval, provided the balance is paid by January 5, and it sends a statement with the remaining balance after each one. If your lender pays through escrow, no paper bill is mailed to you, and the online lookup shows the amount. Wake accepts ACH or eCheck, PayPal, Venmo, Apple Pay, Google Pay and the four major credit cards.

How does revaluation affect a Cary home's tax value?

Wake County reappraised on January 1, 2024, will do so again effective January 1, 2027, and has moved to a two-year cycle after that. State law only requires a reappraisal every eighth year, so Wake revalues far more often than the minimum.

Wake's page describes four steps: neighborhooding, land and building pricing from sales, field and office review, and the notice of assessment with appeal review. It divides about 460,000 parcels into 5,400 neighborhoods and builds a Schedule of Values that the Board of Commissioners must approve. The published schedule for the 2027 round shows results presented to the Board on January 19, 2027, value notices going out by January 22, 2027, and a planned appeal deadline of April 30, 2027.

A homeowner who disputes the notice takes the case to the county's review board. A loss at that board can go to the Property Tax Commission, with notice filed inside 30 days of the mailed decision, as G.S. 105-290 provides. For questions on the 2027 round, Wake runs a call center at 919-857-3800.

What tax relief is available to Cary homeowners?

Wake County administers three state programs for Cary owners in its portion: the Senior and Disabled Program, Tax Deferment and the Disabled Veteran Program. Wake's page says the programs reach low-income owners who are 65 or older, low-income owners who are 100% disabled, and veterans with total and permanent service-connected disability, along with unmarried surviving spouses.

  • Age or disability: $38,800 is the 2026 income limit, and a qualifying home loses whichever is more, $25,000 or half its appraised value, from the taxable amount.
  • Veterans: $45,000 of appraised value is excluded, and the state form sets no age or income test.
  • Circuit breaker: the bill is held to 4.0% of income, or to 5.0% when income runs past $38,800 and up to $58,200, after five years of owning and living in the home.

Wake says the deadline is June 1 under state law, and it considers late applications case by case for good cause through December 31 of that year. Forgetting or not knowing about a program is typically not good cause. Illness, a death in the immediate family, military deployment and delay in getting disability certification are the examples it gives. An owner gets one program, not a stack, so ask the tax office which one fits. See G.S. 105-277.1 for the exclusion rules.

What if I cannot pay my Cary property tax?

Call Wake County Tax Administration at 919-856-5400 before January 6. Wake says it can set up short-term payment plans, that earlier calls leave more options, and that it cannot help once a bill becomes overdue.

State law permits past due taxes to be taken from paychecks, bank accounts or rent, and the lien on the parcel is created by G.S. 105-355 as of the listing date. Foreclosure under G.S. 105-374 finishes with an auction at the courthouse door, though redemption remains possible before confirmation.

If a Cary house also has a mortgage in default, the tax lien and the lender's foreclosure can run at the same time, which narrows the timeline. A sale ahead of any auction leaves the price in the owner's hands, and closing pays the tax out of the proceeds.

What does Cary look like for a seller?

The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate for Cary is 183,582 people, a 5.0% climb from 174,787 in April 2020. It covers 59.23 square miles of land at 2,949.7 people per square mile.

  • Homes owned by their occupants are valued at a median $580,200 (2020-2024), and 66.6% of units are owner-occupied.
  • Gross rent has a median of $1,738.
  • Household income has a median of $134,905.
  • Foreign-born persons: 23.9%; bachelor's degree or higher: 70.5%.

The source for these is the Census Bureau QuickFacts page for Cary town. Check your value notice after each revaluation, since the assessed value is half of the tax calculation. Deeds are filed with the register of deeds of the county that holds the parcel. Wake's register states the excise tax at $2 per thousand dollars of price.

More questions about Cary, NC Property Tax Guide

Which county do I pay Cary property tax to?

Pay the county that holds your parcel: Wake, Chatham or Durham. The Town of Cary says each of the three counties handles assessment, billing and collection for the town's tax, and Wake's page covers the parcels inside its borders.

What is the Cary town property tax rate?

The adopted fiscal year 2027 rate is 36.75 cents per $100 of assessed value, up 2.75 cents. Wake County's rate is 53.71 cents per $100, and Wake collects both for parcels in its portion.

When does Wake County interest begin on Cary taxes?

It starts on January 6, so a payment by January 5 escapes it. Then 2% applies until February 1, followed by three-fourths of a percent each month.

When is the next Wake County revaluation?

The next one takes effect January 1, 2027, and later ones follow every two years. Wake plans to start sending value notices by January 22, 2027.

Can a Cary senior reduce a property tax bill?

Possibly, if age or disability and income tests are met. The exclusion takes off $25,000 or half the value, whichever is larger, and Wake sets a June 1 deadline while weighing late filings for good cause.
